comment: Language-neutral One Router vectors (P0-06 AC-32, DC-7, invariant 6). Every cost is a hand-picked TEST VALUE in seconds, never a mall formula (P0-03 r4 owns those). Positions are (x, z) in metres in one venue frame. Node labels are local to a vector; level, connector, store and place ids are string ids. An edge with twoWay true also adds the reverse edge with the same cost and length. A later server-side router must pass this same file.

vectors.title: Escalator with a horizontal run: the literal RG2 estimate overestimates at F1
Lift with four stops over several levels: one ride (AC-5)

queries.name: O to T by one ride

vectors.title: A connector tuned below the others (E1 at 7 s)
A connector cost of 0: every lift pair at 0 s
A connector cost of 0: E1 at 0 s, so a = 0 and the estimate is 0 (Dijkstra)
Store crossing dearer than its length (7.5 s for 6 m): shortcuts on cross it, off walk round
Store crossing cheaper than its length (4.8 s for 6 m)
The same store Closed: never crossed, shortcuts on or off
A walkway between two buildings' levels with different ordinals (b falls to 0)
A connector whose published cost is lowered (E1 at 13 s, as a preferred mark lowers it)
A walkway cost above 1 s per metre (1.5): a = 1.5, not capped at 1
A destination with two doors: the nearer by straight line costs more, the far one wins
The short way runs against a one-way escalator: the longer legal way (stairs) is returned; the way back rides the escalator
No legal way: only the up escalator, asked to go down; nothing reachable on the goal's level
A two-way escalator (N6) is ridden down; the cheaper one-way one only up
Two buildings joined by the outdoor ground: legs on the outdoor level are marked outdoor
The origin is at a door of the destination: already here
A door node with no edge: the way ends at the nearest reachable node, never a straight segment
The goal is behind a one-way escalator that runs the wrong way; the goal's level has reachable nodes

queries.name: up the reachable side, ending short

vectors.title: Two reachable nodes equally near the goal: the lower cost from the origin wins over the lower index
Equally near and equal cost: the lower node index wins
The nearest reachable point is the origin itself

queries.name: as close as the map can take you

vectors.title: Two equal-cost ways: the lower node index wins, and an equal-cost way is not an other way
Costs 0.1 + 0.2 against 0.3 (floats say 0.30000000000000004 against 0.3): equal, the lower node index wins

queries.name: Costs 0.1 + 0.2 against 0.3 (floats say 0.30000000000000004 against 0.3): equal, the lower node index wins

queries.name: Two ways 0.0004 s apart round to the same millisecond (DC-3): equal, the lower node index wins even though the other is cheaper in floats

vectors.title: Two ways exactly 0.001 s apart are different (DC-3): the cheaper wins whatever its node index

queries.name: Two ways exactly 0.001 s apart are different (DC-3): the cheaper wins whatever its node index

vectors.title: One level, no connectors: the other way bans the lead way's middle edge (edge 2 of 4) and detours round it
A lead way of one edge: that edge is its middle edge and is banned (EC-18)
The destination is itself a walk-through store: the route ends at its door, no crossing leg (shortcuts on)
A routable passage is used on trips to and from the place it serves, whatever the shortcut setting; not as a shortcut elsewhere

to the place behind it, shortcuts on

another trip, shortcuts off: not a shortcut

Two closed passages, listed S2 then S1: the reason lists them in the package's order

Three closed passages, listed S3, S1, S2: the reason lists all three in the package's order

Stairs vs a two-way escalator, exactly routing.stairsSaveS (120 s) apart: the stairs way leads, labelled "Shortest"
